title: Tesla vs Waymo: Who Will Win the Robotaxi Race? | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep. 22
summary: Itay Michaeli argues Tesla needs product renewal and consumer autonomy, while distinguishing its suburban ambitions from Waymo urban robotaxis. Eisman probes earnings, subsidies, valuation and the practical usefulness of autonomy rather than adopting every bullish forecast. The guest approximate 2025 delivery estimate and cheaper-variant expectation receive support. Broad personal autonomy by summer 2026 did not arrive, although the separate robotaxi service progressed. The review also preserves conditional political-demand reasoning, conventional-auto tailwinds and Aptiv valuation analysis without treating sentiment or hypothetical market size as realized investment returns.
assessment: Full transcript read. Most material forecasts are guest views. The broad personal-autonomy summer-2026 expectation misses while the outer 15-month conditional window is still narrowly open at the cutoff. No Tesla stock recommendation is graded from price alone; political and market-size causal stories remain unresolved.
speaker_map_notes: Itay Michaeli provides the sector forecasts and recommendations. Eisman asks skeptical questions, states personal preferences and makes limited explicit propositions; guest bullishness is not imputed to him.
framework_points: Distinguish demand deferral from destruction using regional market-share and category data.
Separate assisted driving, restricted robotaxis and general personal autonomous use.
Challenge terminal-market assumptions and product-cycle extrapolation.
Disaggregate supplier outgrowth into technology content, customer share and mix.
Compare earnings definitions and buyback effects before interpreting valuation compression.
tools_and_charts: County-level EV sales and penetration data
Operational design domains and sensor modalities
US mobility market and lifetime revenue capture model
Supplier growth over market, bookings and backlog
Adjusted versus GAAP earnings and price/earnings ratios
transcript_cautions: Guest identified by metadata as Itay Michaeli; captions distort his name, TD Cowen, Waymo, Aptiv, Visteon and lidar.
Eisman briefly substitutes states for the guest counties in political-adoption data.
Gross and operating margins are initially conflated but clarified in the dialogue.
Ford announcement dates the discussion near mid-August despite August 25 publication; forecast deadlines are interpreted conservatively.
Personal autonomy is distinct from Tesla restricted robotaxi service and from supervised FSD.
